summary: Implement Orpheus security, streaming persistence, startup, title, UI, and stale documentation fixes.
final_report: Implemented the blocking T6 findings in the declared file set. Both chat pages now sanitize marked output through a DOM allowlist before assigning innerHTML, removing non-allowlisted tags, event-handler attributes, unsafe style, and javascript/data href/src values for persisted and streaming assistant content. Turn streaming now persists the accumulated partial buffer in finally while normal completion still finalizes partial=0; the focused SSE regression now asserts streamed partial text survives a provider failure. Home session creation checks response.ok and returned ids, cleans streaming controls and the bubble on failure, displays escaped visible feedback, and returns before /turns. Stop CSS is valid and JS uses grid when showing the control and none when hiding it. Workspace visible title and document title use the exact Sage - <title> separator with textContent/document.title assignments. README now describes the served static UI, lists static pages, and links root serving in the architecture diagram. run.sh installs dependencies only for a fresh virtualenv, keeps startup safe from repeated installs, and makes reload opt-in with RELOAD=1. Python compileall and 14 focused SSE tests pass. bash -n could not run because bash is unavailable on this Windows host; that system error is recorded in oc-issues.txt. Browser verification remains analyzer_pending for Merlin.
notes: Declared exact source, launcher, README, focused test, and job-log file set before editing. Added oc-issues.txt after the shell smoke-check witnessed a missing bash executable, as required for system errors. A later PowerShell line-count probe also failed and was recorded. run.sh now installs requirements only when the virtualenv lacks uvicorn, avoiding repeated startup installs while making fresh environments work; --reload is opt-in via RELOAD=1. Existing shared uncommitted source changes were preserved and these edits were applied on top of them. No other files were intentionally modified.
